name: GA-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Brian Jack running with large financial advantage ($2.0M raised vs $0.15M)
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~6%
No polling or expert ratings available
model.rationale: The baseline of R+16.3 rests on a solid R+15 partisan lean, first-term incumbent Jack's 14-to-1 fundraising edge, and markets at 94% Republican. Keller's minimal war chest gives her no path to close a double-digit structural gap, so I stay near the baseline with a slight nudge toward the fundamentals-only margin.
model.watch: A major outside-spending surge for Keller or a scandal involving Jack could narrow the race, though the district lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Georgia's 3rd District is a solidly Republican seat with a 15-point Republican partisan lean. First-term incumbent Brian Jack is running for reelection and holds an overwhelming financial advantage, having raised about $2.0 million with $1.1 million on hand, while Democrat Maura Keller has raised roughly $150,000. No independent polls or expert ratings are available for this race.

Prediction markets give Republicans about a 94 percent chance of holding the seat, consistent with the district's fundamentals. With no evidence of a competitive environment and the incumbent well positioned, the race is rated Safe Republican, with the main uncertainty being the size of the expected victory margin rather than the outcome.
